messages:
maya: FYI privacy escalated: a DSAR audit trail showed a missing delete-attempt entry for a user yesterday. Investigating whether RBAC or KMS changes suppressed audit logs. Anyone seen anomalies overnight? :thinking:
oliver: I saw an IAM rollout for `keystore-worker` yesterday morning that added `roles/storage.admin` scoped oddly to the bucket prefix. That could have bypassed uniform bucket-level audit metadata. PR: #4905.
samir: Checking audit logs now. I can confirm `storage.objects.delete` was logged for some objects, but the corresponding `keystore.delete_request` custom event from our service was absent for ~10 entries. Timing lines up with the IAM change. Example log snippet: ```protoPayload.methodName: "storage.objects.delete" resourceName: "projects/_/buckets/priv-evidence/objects/dsar-123"```\njordan: Legal note: we need the service-level assertion for attempted deletes (who requested, request id, hash). If the service event is missing we can't assert the deletion happened. We may need to treat those DSARs as not completed until evidence is reconstructed.
maya: Root cause hypothesis: the IAM binding granted broad storage roles to the worker service account which caused object writes to bypass our service's audit wrapper that signs evidence blobs. Also hash metadata was lost because we relied on ACL-preserved metadata that isn't preserved under the new uniform settings.
legal: If true, we should pause auto-closures and treat affected DSARs as "awaiting-evidence". Also open an audit retention exception for the 7 affected requests. We'll need a log of the exact request ids and timestamps.
ops-bot: alert: keystore-worker IAM change detected by config-audit (change_id=cfg-20260218-02) 
oliver: Plan: 1) revert the overly-broad IAM grant (rollback PR) 2) add a conditional binding scoped to the single object path prefix with `roles/storage.objectCreator` only, 3) re-run evidence forwarder to rehydrate missing metadata where possible. Will prep PR for 1 & 2.
samir: Rehydration step: pull DLQ + object rewrite job can attach signed assertion with `priv-evidence` service account. Example rewrite command: ```gsutil cp -a private -h "x-goog-meta-sig:$(gcloud kms sign --key=priv-evidence-key --plaintext=hash)" gs://priv-evidence/tmp/dsar-123 gs://priv-evidence/dsar-123```\. We need to ensure KMS key permissions permit signing by `priv-evidence` service account.
jordan: Legal: approved rehydration as long as we clearly annotate which artifacts were reconstructed and include a note in the evidence blob that it was backfilled with timestamps and operator id. We also require an immutable flag and retention 90 days.
maya: Security asks: add a short-lived conditional IAM binding instead of broad role, add an audit-sink that captures our service assertions to BigQuery, and lock down the KMS key so only `priv-evidence` SA can sign, not encrypt.
oliver: Will open PR to revoke `roles/storage.admin` from `keystore-worker@...` and instead grant `roles/storage.objectCreator` on `projects/_/buckets/priv-evidence` with condition `resource.name.startsWith("projects/_/buckets/priv-evidence/objects/dsar-")`.
legal: Also request a retention-exception ticket template so we can track impacted customers and remedy steps. I'll file one after we have the list.
samir: One more wrinkle: during the KMS rotation last month we changed key policy to permit `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign` for a group that includes devtools; that might allow reconstruction without proper separation. We should tighten key IAM to `serviceAccount:priv-evidence@...` only.
maya: Ok, urgent action list: - oliver: revert & minimal IAM PR + justification (target within 30m) - samir: run DLQ scan and produce CSV of affected dsar_ids/timestamps/hashes (ETA 1h) - jordan/legal: prepare retention-exception ticket and customer comms draft (ETA 2h) - ops-bot: add alert for `keystore.evidence.missing > 0 for 10m` -> pager duty to eng-security and privacy-oncall
deploy-bot: rollback started for PR #4905 (target=keystore-worker role change)
oliver: Rollback completed. New PR #4910 created to grant minimal conditional role. Link: https://git.internal/pull/4910
samir: DLQ scan complete: produced `missing-evidence-20260218.csv` with 7 entries. Uploading to secure ticket. Command used: `gcloud pubsub subscriptions pull dsar-keystore-dlq --limit=100 --format=json > missing.json` then parsing.
jordan: Evidence backfill runbook step written. It includes: verify DLQ hash, sign with KMS (priv-evidence SA), push to `priv-evidence` with metadata `backfilled=true signed_by=priv-evidence@...`, and append reconciliation entry in the DSAR tracker.
legal: Retention-exception ticket created: TICKET-8429. Noting temporary exception for evidence immutability for these backfilled items until 90 days.
maya: Postmortem will include: how IAM change got approved, why audits didn't catch the wrapper bypass, and tighten preflight tests for evidence write path. Schedule 72h postmortem meeting.
oliver: I'll also add a CI check that deploys a synthetic DSAR evidence write and verifies audit sink receives the service assertion before the IAM change can be merged.
samir: Follow-up: we should add a KMS integration test for sign-only access and ensure rotation doesn't include broad groups.
maya: Great. Closing loop: once evidence is backfilled and legal signs off, we can close the DSARs and mark incident resolved. Keep posting status here. :white_check_mark:
